dataset: Real clinical cohort, postmenopausal ER+/HER2- patients not receiving chemotherapy
metrics: Performed 'similarly' to NHG (non-superiority-flavored result)
main_result: AI risk stratification performs comparably to, but not clearly better than, an existing simple grading system
limitations: Authors call for further prospective validation
research_gap: Honest negative/neutral finding: not every AI model beats the simple existing clinical tool
notes: Useful negative/neutral result reinforcing the project brief's caution against assuming AI/deep learning automatically outperforms simpler existing clinical tools (Section 1).

title: Using natural language processing to construct a metastatic breast cancer cohort from linked cancer registry and electronic medical records data
authors: Ling AY, Kurian AW, Caswell-Jin JL, et al.
problem: Semi-supervised NLP + linked cancer registry + EMR to identify recurrent metastatic breast cancer cases
dataset: Linked California Cancer Registry + Stanford EMR (per prior literature; not independently re-confirmed this session)
target: Recurrent metastatic breast cancer case identification
baselines: NLP-derived features alone vs NLP+registry combined
metrics: NLP-derived features alone were as informative as NLP+registry combined for identifying recurrent metastatic cases
main_result: NLP alone matches NLP+registry performance for cohort identification
limitations: UNKNOWN
research_gap: Useful precedent for registry-linked EHR cohort building methodology
notes: CLASSIFICATION: DETECTION/cohort-construction, not prediction. Same Stanford Kurian/Caswell-Jin lineage as P0003/P0005/P0009.

title: Universal Abstraction: Harnessing Frontier Models to Structure Real-World Data at Scale (UniMedAbstractor/UMA)
problem: Zero-shot LLM abstraction framework (GPT-4o) to structure real-world oncology data at scale
dataset: Providence Health System (large integrated delivery network) real-world EHR
target: N/A (extraction/abstraction framework, not an outcome predictor)
metrics: UMA+GPT-4o beat conventional baselines by ~2 absolute points in F1/accuracy
main_result: LLM zero-shot abstraction modestly outperforms conventional baselines at large real-world health-system scale
limitations: UNPUBLISHED preprint - not peer reviewed, treat as provisional
research_gap: Large real-world health system directly relevant to 'LLM extracting structured variables from oncology notes'
notes: CAUTION: unreviewed arXiv preprint. Should not be cited as validated evidence until peer-reviewed. Include for awareness of the LLM-extraction frontier only.
